items.prompt:
A job interview calls for:
A) formal English
B) slang
C) silence

Talking casually with friends is:
A) informal speech
B) always formal
C) not allowed

Formal speech avoids:
A) slang
B) standard grammar
C) clear words

In a presentation, 'So yeah, this stuff is basically super important' should become:
A) 'This issue is critically important.'
B) 'This stuff's a big deal, trust me.'
C) 'Yeah, it's major.'

When is INFORMAL speech appropriate?
A) in casual settings like talking with friends
B) in a formal debate
C) in a job interview
items.answer: A) in casual settings like talking with friends

solution.answer: A) in casual settings like talking with friends

items.prompt:
Adapting your speech to context means:
A) matching your register to the audience and situation
B) always using slang
C) always speaking the same way
items.answer: A) matching your register to the audience and situation

steps: Fit the setting. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) matching your register to the audience and situation

items.prompt:
Which sentence is MOST appropriate for a formal college-admissions interview?
A) 'I'm eager to contribute to your research community.'
B) 'Yeah, your school seems pretty cool.'
C) 'So basically I just wanna get in.'
items.answer: A) 'I'm eager to contribute to your research community.'

steps: Formal, complete, no slang. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) 'I'm eager to contribute to your research community.'

items.prompt:
Why is being able to switch between formal and informal English valuable?
A) different contexts call for different registers, and using the right one is effective
B) formal is always better everywhere
C) informal is never useful
items.answer: A) different contexts call for different registers, and using the right one is effective

steps: Match register to context. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) different contexts call for different registers, and using the right one is effective
